title: Lexicographically Smallest Generated String
summary: Given two strings, str1 and str2, of lengths n and m respectively, generate a string word of length n + m - 1 that meets the following conditions for each index 0 <= i <= n - 1: - If str1[i] is 'T', the substring of word starting at index i and of length m must be equal to str2, i.e., word[i..(i + m - 1)] == str2.
statement: Given two strings, str1 and str2, of lengths n and m respectively, generate a string word of length n + m - 1 that meets the following conditions for each index 0 <= i <= n - 1: - If str1[i] is 'T', the substring of word starting at index i and of length m must be equal to str2, i.e., word[i..(i + m - 1)] == str2. - If str1[i] is 'F', the substring of word starting at index i and of length m must not be equal to str2, i.e., word[i..(i + m - 1)] != str2. Return the lexicographically smallest string that can be generated by str1 and str2. If no such string can be generated, return an empty string "".
constraints: str1 contains T and F flags and str2 is a nonempty lowercase pattern.
The result length is len(str1)+len(str2)-1; a T window must equal str2 and an F window must differ.
Return the lexicographically smallest valid result, or an empty string if constraints conflict.
hints: T windows force letters; all other positions should begin as a, and an equal F window must be broken as far right as possible.
Apply and consistency-check every forced pattern copy, then scan forbidden windows left to right.
When an F window still equals the pattern, change its rightmost unfixed position to b; fail if every position is fixed.
Changing the latest possible free position preserves the earliest lexicographic prefix, and earlier processed windows cannot be restored by that change.
editorial: Changing the latest possible free position preserves the earliest lexicographic prefix, and earlier processed windows cannot be restored by that change.

tests.explanation: Forced T windows and the smallest changes for F windows produce ababa.
The overlapping forced copies require incompatible letters, so no result exists.
